headline: High-risk workspace and command overlap: Cursor can write/egress broadly while Rasa handles external chat channels, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard, and can use MCP; Rasa ingests messages from external chat channels. If Rasa content is copied into Cursor or bridged through shared files/MCP, attacker-controlled text can steer Cursor. The pairwise bridge is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Rasa messages are copied into Cursor buffers or files
IF an MCP server or shared workspace relays Rasa content into Cursor without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the tools during review
Use a separate workspace directory for Cursor and Rasa artifacts
Add a provenance prefix to any imported Rasa text
Turn off MCP servers that can ingest chat content
requires-engineering: enforce content provenance tags at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and has broad network egress; Rasa handles text and voice from external channels. If sensitive support transcripts or code are moved into Cursor, either agent can expose them beyond the intended boundary. The profiles show a plausible shared-data path, but not a direct leak channel, so medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF support transcripts containing sensitive data are opened in Cursor
IF Cursor sends copied workspace content to external model providers
mitigations: Keep support transcripts out of Cursor workspaces
Redact secrets before copying text between tools
Restrict Cursor to a non-sensitive repo clone
Review outbound API destinations for both tools
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and shares state via the local filesystem across instances; Rasa is a chatbot framework that can also be deployed alongside shared project assets. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can collide without locking. The overlap is dangerous by default in shared development setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Cursor and Rasa operate on the same repository or workspace
IF either agent writes generated files or commits without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files
Use git branches per agent
Add a manual lock file before writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write serialization

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code or edits from its agent loop, and Rasa can surface those outputs to users through chat channels. If Rasa treats Cursor-produced text as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect support responses or bad operational actions. The profiles imply an input-to-output chain, but not a fully automated action path, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated text is pasted into Rasa responses without review
IF Rasa automation forwards Cursor output to end users
mitigations: Require human review before Rasa sends Cursor-derived content
Mark Cursor output as untrusted in the handoff
Limit Rasa to templated replies for edited content
Add a verification checklist for factual claims
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that sends data to model providers and handles workspace files, while Rasa routes text and voice through messaging platforms. If regulated support data or EU PII is processed in Cursor and then forwarded through Rasa channels, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify a direct mismatch, so medium reflects the plausible compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is edited in Cursor and then sent through Rasa channels
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not configured in either tool
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Cursor sessions
Document retention settings for each channel
Route sensitive cases to a separate workflow
Review vendor DPAs and residency terms
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing by data class
